evals.name: full-migration-kata
evals.prompt: The app in this directory uses Recoil and we're done with it. Migrate the whole thing to Jotai 3 — jotai, jotai-family, jotai-loadable and fast-deep-equal are already in node_modules, no network needed. When you're finished `npm run check` (tsc + vitest) must pass and no file under src/ may import 'recoil'. Keep behaviour identical: the theme must still persist under the same localStorage key, resetting the thermostat must still work, the search family must not re-create atoms on every render, and the user from the server props must still land in state before the first render.
evals.expected_output: src/ fully on Jotai: npm run check passes, zero 'recoil' imports; searchResultsFamily uses atomFamily with a deep-equal areEqual; themeAtom is atomWithStorage with key 'app_theme' and validation; tempFahrenheit handles RESET; userAtom is hydrated via useHydrateAtoms inside the Provider; loadable/unwrap atoms created at module level; refresh via atomWithRefresh or a tick atom; tests ported to createStore.
expectations: `npm run typecheck` exits 0 after the migration
`npm run test` exits 0 after the migration with the same five test cases still present
No file under src/ imports from 'recoil' (grep returns nothing) and package.json no longer lists recoil as a dependency
The search family is an atomFamily (jotai-family) created with an areEqual comparator (fast-deep-equal or equivalent), so object parameters are compared by value
The theme atom uses atomWithStorage with the storage key 'app_theme' and still validates stored values
The fahrenheit writable atom accepts RESET and resetting it restores 20°C (test or component evidence)
The server-provided user is hydrated with useHydrateAtoms (or an equivalent store.set before first render) inside the Jotai Provider, not with a useEffect after mount
Loadable/unwrap wrapper atoms are defined once at module level, never inside a component body
The posts refresh is implemented with atomWithRefresh or a tick atom read inside the async read, and the refresh button still triggers a refetch
The transcript shows the inventory script was run (or an equivalent dependency analysis) before editing

evals.name: plan-only-no-edits
evals.prompt: We are considering moving this app off Recoil to Jotai but nobody on the team has done it before. Don't change any code yet. Analyse the state layer in src/ and tell me: how many atoms/selectors/families there are, which ones are risky and why, what order you'd migrate them in, and which decisions you need from me before starting.
evals.expected_output: A written analysis with no source changes: 17 features (7 atoms, 7 selectors, 2 atomFamilies, 1 selectorFamily); risks named (object-param selectorFamily, effect-backed theme atom with storage layout, initializeState hydration, loadable consumers, DefaultValue reset, waitForAll/noWait); an order (free features, then small components); explicit decisions (Jotai 2 vs 3, storage layout, SSR/hydration seam, jotai-family).
expectations: No file under src/ was modified (git status clean apart from generated report files)
The analysis reports 17 Recoil features with the correct breakdown: 7 atoms, 7 selectors, 2 atomFamilies, 1 selectorFamily (or 19 nodes when the two nested default selectors are counted separately)
searchResultsFamily is called out as risky because its parameter is an object compared by value in Recoil and by reference in Jotai
themeAtom's localStorage effect is called out AND the analysis states, in so many words, that the storage key and JSON layout must be preserved so existing users keep their data (quote the sentence)
The RecoilRoot initializeState hydration of userAtom is identified and a useHydrateAtoms-based seam is proposed

The proposed order never moves a feature while a feature that reads it (or that it reads) is still on the other runtime without naming the bridge — walk each step's scope against the dependency edges in src/state; a step that moves settingsAtom before dashboardSelector without a bridge fails
The response asks the user to decide the target Jotai major version (2 vs 3) before starting
The response lists the Loadable consumers (useRecoilValueLoadable/useRecoilStateLoadable, valueMaybe, .contents) as call sites that change shape
The analysis warns that an atomWithRefresh setter must be called with no argument (onClick={refresh} would pass the click event), or otherwise flags the refresh wiring in Posts.tsx as a change point
The analysis notices that jotai and its companion packages sit in devDependencies and must move to dependencies before shipping

evals.name: incremental-two-components
evals.prompt: Start our Recoil → Jotai migration with the smallest safe slice: move the counter state (counterAtom, doubleSelector) and the thermostat state (tempCelsiusAtom, tempFahrenheitSelector) to Jotai, and leave everything else on Recoil for now — both libraries will coexist for a while. `npm run check` must stay green and the existing tests for those selectors must keep passing on Jotai.
evals.expected_output: Both runtimes mounted (Jotai Provider inside/alongside RecoilRoot); exactly those four features on Jotai with Counter.tsx and Thermostat.tsx updated; tempFahrenheit handles RESET so useResetAtom works; the counter helper hook typed with PrimitiveAtom; the relevant tests ported to createStore while the other tests still run on Recoil; npm run check passes; the remaining 13 features untouched.
expectations: `npm run check` exits 0 after the change
counterAtom, doubleSelector, tempCelsiusAtom and tempFahrenheitSelector are defined with jotai and no longer with recoil; all other state files still use recoil
A Jotai Provider is mounted so that components using both runtimes work (RecoilRoot is still present)
The fahrenheit atom's write function handles RESET (typeof RESET in its argument type or an explicit RESET branch) and Thermostat uses useResetAtom
Counter.tsx's helper hook parameter type changed from RecoilState<number> to a Jotai atom type (PrimitiveAtom<number> or WritableAtom)
The double/fahrenheit tests run against a Jotai store (createStore / store.set / store.get) while the user/todo/posts tests remain on snapshot_UNSTABLE
No file other than the two state files, the two components, App/provider wiring and the test file was changed
The transcript shows the agent checked dependencies (inventory or equivalent) and explained why these four features need no bridge
